# Edmund Carrow

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Family:** [Izzy](../character/izzy.md) (sibling)

## Appearance

Edmund Carrow possesses well-shaped features and straight black hair. He is noted for his large, magnificent gray eyes, which feature deep recesses that radiate an unusual fascination.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P12](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0012), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P13](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0013), [v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS WINIFRED INTERVENES P25](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0025)_

## Personality

Edmund Carrow possesses an imaginative, absent-minded, and somewhat theatrical personality, and he holds a deep adoration for ghost stories. He exhibits a sense of responsibility by personally assuming the fault for others. Driven by an aspiration to become a poet, he actively composes poetry and also demonstrates a capacity for praying fantastically. His personal motivations include defending his mother and [Grace Ashdown](../character/grace.md) from insults, fulfilling his duty to redeem his honor, traveling to the Nile to see the sphinx, and traveling to [Kettlebridge](../codex/places.md#kettlebridge) to have a tooth pulled. He is deeply adverse to seeing others in pain or injured, which fills him with an overwhelming urge to run away from their sight and hearing.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P24](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0024), [v5 CHAPTER VIII. ## History

From the moment he learned to read, Edmund Carrow adored poets and spent hours reading their work, even winning a school award for composing a verse. He frequently gathered with the other children in [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), where he mused poetically, read myths, and imagined the Pied Piper leading the boys away. After [Dan Coyle](../character/coyle.md) taunted his family, Edmund bravely challenged Dan to a fight at school; despite his dread, he fiercely defeated Dan, forcing him to retract his insults. On his way home from the fight, Edmund was praised by Mr. Ashdown for defending the honor of women before having his bruises tended to by [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md).

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P4](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0004), [v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P7](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0007), [v5 CHAPTER III. ## Quotes

> "Being injured is something I despise, and it would cause great suffering. My decision to depart must be made by me first, as Father mentioned he would not force my leaving until then."
>
> — Edmund Carrow — [v5 CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT P14](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0014)

> "However, I do not intend to feel scared again, sir. Experiencing fear about troubles is more unpleasant than those troubles are. I plan to request that father drive me to Kettlebridge tomorrow so I can have my tooth pulled."
>
> — Edmund Carrow — [v5 CHAPTER XVII. A DOUBLE VICTORY P71](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0071)

> "The angel of flowers has traveled across the earth today, summoning the blossoms. Those blue wings of his are visible to me on that hill near the forest."
>
> — Edmund Carrow — [v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P20](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0020)

> "The angels of the flowers are not. A pale, misty blue describes them, exactly like the valley's haze. Oh, my desire to fly is so strong. Glorious it must be."
>
> — Edmund Carrow — [v5 CHAPTER III. THE HOLLOWMERE CHILDREN P22](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0022)

> "They wish for me to—yet I am unable to. The pain would be immense."
>
> — Edmund Carrow — [v5 CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT P11](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0011)

## Relationships

### [Coyle](../character/coyle.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/coyle--edmund-carrow.md)

Edmund and [Dan Coyle](../character/coyle.md) are enemies following a personal conflict. After Dan taunted [Grace](../character/grace.md) and Mrs. [Carrow](../character/carrow.md), Edmund challenged him to a fight to defend their honor. Edmund fiercely brawled with Dan at school, ultimately defeating him and forcing Dan to retract his insults.

### [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/edmund-carrow--john-ashdown.md)
